title: The 5 Biggest Betrayals in History
hook_prompt: a dagger hidden behind a smiling Roman senator, dramatic oil painting, dark cinematic lighting

entries.title: Benedict Arnold sells West Point
entries.text: A celebrated general of the American Revolution, Arnold secretly plotted to hand the fort of West Point to the British. The plan collapsed when his contact, Major John André, was caught with the plans hidden in his boot. Arnold fled to the British, and his name became America's word for traitor.
entries.prompt: 18th century American general secretly passing documents to a British officer at night, dramatic oil painting

entries.title: Mir Jafar at the Battle of Plassey
entries.text: Mir Jafar commanded much of the Nawab of Bengal's army, but made a secret deal with the British East India Company. At Plassey, his troops stood by and refused to fight. The British won, made him a puppet ruler, and began 190 years of rule over India.
entries.image_query: Lord Clive meeting Mir Jafar after the Battle of Plassey Hayman
entries.prompt: British officer shaking hands with an Indian nobleman after a battle, 1757, dramatic oil painting

entries.title: Judas Iscariot
entries.text: One of the twelve apostles, Judas agreed to hand Jesus over to the authorities for thirty pieces of silver. He pointed him out in the garden of Gethsemane with a kiss. Two thousand years later, a 'Judas kiss' still means betrayal disguised as friendship.
entries.prompt: the kiss of Judas in a dark garden at night, torches, Renaissance oil painting

entries.title: Brutus and the Ides of March
entries.text: Julius Caesar spared Brutus after the civil war and treated him almost like a son. On the Ides of March, Brutus joined the senators who stabbed Caesar 23 times. They wanted to save the Roman Republic. Instead, it fell to an emperor.
entries.prompt: assassination of Julius Caesar in the Roman senate, senators with daggers, dramatic oil painting

entries.title: Hitler betrays Stalin
entries.text: In 1939, Hitler and Stalin signed a non-aggression pact and split Eastern Europe between them. On 22 June 1941, Germany broke it and invaded with over 3 million soldiers. The war that followed killed around 27 million Soviet citizens.
entries.prompt: two dictators shaking hands over a map of Europe, tanks in the shadows, dramatic oil painting, no symbols
